messages:
Avery Johnson: Just wrapped our first official customer reference call (Northwind) w/ a late-stage Dedicated prospect. Quick debrief here while it’s fresh.

Avery Johnson: What went well: 
- Northwind’s VP Eng was super credible + specific about why they moved (latency consistency + predictable throughput)
- They handled the “why not just use hosted X?” question really cleanly
- The prospect lit up on the fallback/routing + “graceful degradation” story :thumbsup:

Stephanie Nguyen: +1. Also Northwind was willing to speak to operational reality (on-call, SLOs) vs fluffy “AI transformation” stuff. That landed.

Rachel Kim: From CS side: Northwind felt prepared and not overburdened. Good pacing, and we didn’t get into any weird escalation history. Big win.

Miguel Santos: Agree. They liked having a clear “what to emphasize” section. But we missed a couple things in the brief that would’ve prevented awkward moments.

Markus Klein: Yeah. Biggest gap: we didn’t pre-validate the prospect’s technical context. Prospect was on multi-region + asked about cross-region failover specifics. Northwind answered generally, but we didn’t have a crisp Redwood-approved statement queued.

Soojin Lee: Noted. We should add a standard “approved claim language” callout in the brief (esp on reliability/fallback + SLAs) so customers aren’t improvising.

Avery Johnson: Missing prep / awkward bits:
- Prospect asked for exact p95 numbers + $/1M tokens. Northwind hesitated (they’re ok with ranges publicly, but not exacts on live calls). We should’ve warned them what to do.
- I didn’t give Northwind enough detail on who the prospect was / what stage / their current provider. They asked mid-call “what are you using today?” and it got clunky.

Camila Reyes: This is consistent with what we said in kickoff—customer shouldn’t be surprised. We need the brief template to force the requestor to include: prospect stage, current stack/provider (if known), and “top 3 questions we expect.”

Isabelle Laurent: Also… we need a better post-call logging checklist. Right now it’s too optional. If we want influence reporting, the AE needs to tag the deal + log that the reference happened.

Tyler Benson: +1. I can update the brief template today. Can someone paste the exact questions that caught us flat-footed?

Avery Johnson: Questions that came up:
1) “What’s your p95 at 1k / 4k context, and how stable is it during traffic spikes?”
2) “Did you do Dedicated or Private? Why not VPC?”
3) “How do you handle capacity crunch—do requests fail or downgrade?”
4) “What’s your monthly token volume + unit cost change?” (we should steer away)

Markus Klein: Add “how to answer safely” guidance:
- If asked for exact metrics: offer % improvement / ranges + say “we can share more in 1:1 under NDA”
- If asked about competitor: keep it high-level, no vendor-bashing
- If asked about pricing: hard no

Rachel Kim: And add an “avoid list” per customer. For Northwind: avoid mentioning the September latency spike incident. They brought it up themselves when asked about stability (not terrible, but we didn’t want that to be the headline).

Camila Reyes: Action items I’m hearing:
1) Update brief template to include: prospect context + stage, expected Qs, hard-no topics (pricing, exact costs), and “if asked for exact metrics -> talk in ranges” guidance
2) Add section: “Approved Redwood statements” (reliability/fallback/SLA language)
3) Add post-call checklist + HubSpot fields to log reference usage
4) Add a pre-call 10 min alignment w/ AE + CSM + customer (day-of) to remove surprises

Tyler Benson: I’ll take (1) + (4) for the template. Will drop a v2 in Drive and post link here for comments.

Isabelle Laurent: I’ll draft the HubSpot logging steps + what fields to update (deal tag + reference customer name + date). Will share in #sales once we align.

Soojin Lee: I’ll provide a short “approved language” snippet for fallbacks + reliability + Dedicated vs Private framing. Keep it tight so customers can literally read it if needed.

Stephanie Nguyen: Also: who’s the call host? We let it drift a bit. Next time I want a clear timekeeper + “parking lot” for deep technical questions -> follow-up w/ SE.

Markus Klein: Happy to join future calls as SE shadow when it’s a Private/VPC-heavy prospect. For Dedicated calls, a short escalation path in the brief would help (“if asked about X, point to Markus/SE follow-up”).

Avery Johnson: Awesome. Net-net: call was still a win, prospect asked for security review follow-up and sent over their high-level requirements right after.

Camila Reyes: Great. Once Tyler drops v2, I’ll socialize to Marketing + CS so we standardize. Let’s try to have the updated template in place before the next reference call this week.

Tyler Benson: Will do. EOD draft coming. :writing_hand:
